narrative: The model estimated a 69% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That high predicted risk is why your law school application was denied. The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This very low third-year rank pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 20, well below the accepted-student average of about 37, and it also pushed toward failure. The third factor, your lower-middle family income bracket, leaned modestly toward passing, but it was not strong enough to offset the academic indicators. To improve future chances, focus on the areas the decision weighted most: prepare for and retake the LSAT, and take steps to demonstrate stronger academic performance, such as additional coursework or a structured explanation of any circumstances affecting your grades. Meet with an admissions advisor, ask for feedback, and reapply only after these indicators have improved.
